gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false lower bound for non-first members of an unfiltered batch: only the batch-start choice satisfies the weak-greedy condition, while later members use stale surrogates and need not satisfy the claimed diagonal bound.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed per-member diagonal lower bound incorrectly transfers the batch-start weak-greedy guarantee to non-first batch elements selected using a frozen or stale residual.

component_coverage.gold_component: The full-row diagonal lower bound is invalid because only the first batch member satisfies the weak-greedy condition and later members are selected from a stale surrogate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that non-first batch elements have zero residual in the frozen batch space, gives a counterexample to the claimed bound, and attributes the failure to the stale batch update and choice rule.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns false batch product inequalities and resulting batch-dependent rate claims. It does not identify the distinct induction defect in which constants evaluated at an auxiliary index are incorrectly replaced by constants at the failure index despite opposite monotonicity.

ISSUE-003 also rejects the stated batching rate-loss factor, but its diagnosis is that the batch algorithm has a b-dependent asymptotic rate due to the false product inequality. It does not identify the algebraic error of replacing minimum-defined constants by one branch without establishing that branch is active.

ISSUE-004 identifies the false Banach product inequality inherited from the batch diagonal-bound defect. It does not diagnose the separate Case 2 arithmetic comparison q<L≤Ls implying Ls+q≥2Ls, nor the resulting failure of the exponent contradiction.
